finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> endpoint returns any invoice by ID with no ownership check and no authentication. This is an IDOR. The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> does enforce an owner check, which shows the check was intended.
finding.source: inv_id URL path parameter, controlled by any requester (even unauthenticated)
finding.sink: jsonify(inv), which returns the full invoice record of any customer

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator or before_request hook
INVOICES.get(inv_id) fetches the record by ID alone, with no customer scoping
The full record is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No comparison against g.user, no login_required decorator, and no before_request hook in the file. Compared with get_my_invoice at lines 16-17, which does compare inv['customer'] to g.user['id']. Cannot see whether an external app-level auth layer exists, but no ownership check exists anywhere on this path.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator or before_request hook and returns INVOICES.get(inv_id) via jsonify with no owner check, unlike the check at invoices.py:16 in the sibling route; the file is the only one in the directory, so no external auth layer is visible.
